source_title: LTC6268-10/LTC6269-10 data sheet (as above) and LT Journal of Analog Innovation V25N2 article 'Op Amp Combines Femtoamp Bias Current with 4GHz Gain Bandwidth Product, Shines New Light on Photonics Applications'

figure_table: data sheet Figures 6 and 7; LT Journal Figures 5(a)-(c) and 6
resistor_size: not stated for this case; the LT Journal photo (Fig. 5c) puts it at position R9 of the 3-channel board, which is a 1206 footprint in the DC2414A Rev 3 schematic (cross-reference, not stated in the data sheet)
amplifier_and_package: LTC6268-10, SOT-23 on the board of LT Journal Fig. 5c
layout: field-shunting ground trace between the resistor pads, 'much wider than that used in the case of the LTC6268, extending under the entire resistor dielectric'; resistor on the bottom side, feedback trace 'entirely shielded' (LT Journal Fig. 5c caption)
board_material_thickness: not stated in these documents; the DC2414A manual gives Nelco N4000-EP-SI, relative permittivity 3.4
quantity: total feedback capacitance, upper bound
value_as_stated: upper limit Cf = 1/(2pi x 402kOhm x 34MHz) = 11.6fF; LT Journal: 'reduced feedback capacitance from approximately 100fF ... to 11.6fF'
how_obtained: inferred from a measured 10.3-ns total system rise time (34 MHz), assuming the whole bandwidth limit is feedback capacitance, which the source itself calls 'not fair' (so an upper bound)
verification: read on rendered PDF pages (data sheet pp. 14-15; LT Journal PDF pp. 3-4, including the board photograph of Figure 5(c))
notes: Reduction from about 100 fF to at most 11.6 fF, a factor of 8 or more, by shielding alone (and possibly a larger resistor body). LT Journal Fig. 5c also shows a 'much lighter dose' of shielding at R12. The LT Journal caption gives the permittivity of FR4 and ceramic as 'typically 5', the data sheet caption as 'typically 4'.

source_title: Demo Manual DC2414A (as above)
resistor_value: R9 = 10 MOhm (assembly A) or 1 MOhm (assembly B); 9.76 MOhm in the Figure 3 example
layout: 'very low C' channel U1: R_F on the bottom side with a 'rather extreme' grounded copper shield under the resistor

value_as_stated: approximately 7fF, 'a simplification, derived from the fact that at 10M of gain, that channel achieves rise times as low as 100ns'
how_obtained: stated; inferred by the manufacturer from rise time. With the single-pole relation, 100 ns at 10 MOhm gives 1/(2 pi x 10 MOhm x 3.5 MHz) = 4.5 fF (this survey's arithmetic), so the quoted 7 fF is not a direct single-pole conversion
frequency_or_bandwidth: about 3.5 MHz (100 ns rise) at 10 MOhm
verification: read on rendered PDF pages

source_title: Reference Design Maximizing Transimpedance Bandwidth for LIDAR and Time-of-Flight Applications (TIDA-060025), with its BOM, schematic and layer plots
document_number: TIDUEL3A; BOM TIDRXT2; schematic TIDRXT3; assembly TIDRXT4; layer plots TIDRXT6
revision_date: November 2018, revised April 2022 (board REV E1, BOM generated 11/12/2018)
figure_table: Figure 2-7 (simulation schematic with 75 fF), Figure 4-1 (schematic), Table 3-1 (rise/fall times), BOM items 14 and 43
resistor_size: 0201 (Yageo RC0201FR-074K99L, thick film), two in series
resistor_value: 2 x 4.99 kOhm (R46, R48), each in parallel with a 0.15-pF 0201 thin-film capacitor (AVX 02011JR15ZBSTR, C28, C30)
amplifier_and_package: OPA858IDSG, WSON-8 (2 mm x 2 mm) with FB pin; feedback parts on the same (bottom) side next to the pins
layout: six-layer board; schematic note 'Cut out planes under input and output pins'; the layer plots show plane cut-outs under the TIA input, feedback network and output on all four inner planes (GND L2, 3.3 V L3, 5 V L4, GND L5) and the surface pour cleared around the TIA
board_material_thickness: not stated in the documents read
quantity: total feedback capacitance (design value, two equal sections in series); measured edges compared with TI's simulation
value_as_stated: required feedback capacitance 'approximately 100 fF' for Q = 0.707 (205 MHz) and '75 fF' for Q = 0.95 (260 MHz), TIDUEL3A p. 6; built as 2 x (4.99 kOhm || 0.15 pF) in series = 75 fF nominal; simulation schematic Figure 2-7 (p. 8) uses 10 kOhm || 75 fF with a 1.1-pF diode
how_obtained: design value and TINA-TI simulation by TI; Table 3-1 (p. 14) gives simulated 90-10 % fall 1.20 ns and 10-90 % rise 1.18 ns, measured (100-ns pulse) fall 1.11 ns and rise 1.68 ns; TI attributes the slower rise to the laser driver's turn-off. This survey calibrated a second-order TIA model (single-pole op amp) to TI's simulated edges and solved for the C_F that reproduces each measured edge: fall edges give 65-66 fF (51-72 fF for GBW 4.5-6.5 GHz and C_T 1.7-2.1 pF); rise edges would need 115-117 fF
frequency_or_bandwidth: target > 200 MHz at 10 kOhm (260 MHz predicted at Q = 0.95)
verification: design values (p. 6), Figure 2-7 (p. 8), Table 3-1 (p. 14), schematic and note (p. 18), BOM (TIDRXT2 p. 1) and layer plots (TIDRXT6) read on rendered PDF pages; the C_F values reproducing the edges are this survey's inference (scripts_archive/parasitic_cf/inferred_feedback_c.py)
confidence: high for the design facts; low for the inferred values (laser and photodiode speed, capacitor tolerance, GBW and C_T are not known well enough to resolve a few tens of fF)
notes: TI's own worked example of the 'two series resistors below 0.15 pF' rule. The amplifier-limited (fall) edge is slightly faster than TI simulated with exactly 75 fF, so no excess capacitance from the two 0201 resistors, their pads, the traces or the FB-to-IN- package coupling is visible in this plane-cut layout; with an unknown tolerance on the 0.15-pF capacitors (not given in the BOM) the data bound that excess only loosely, to a few tens of fF at most. The schematic also shows a 10-Ohm resistor (R50) between the feedback node and IN- (pin 3), as the OPA855 data sheet (p. 30) recommends 10-20 Ohm of isolation at the inverting input.

source_title: Noise spectra in balanced optical detectors based on transimpedance amplifiers
authors: A. V. Masalov, A. Kuzhamuratov, A. I. Lvovsky
resistor_value: 12 kOhm (C_F = 0 and 0.3 pF), 4.3 kOhm (0.3 pF), 2 kOhm (0.4 pF)
amplifier_and_package: TI OPA847 (package not stated); two Hamamatsu S5972 photodiodes
layout: follows Kumar et al. (2012) 'with an improved circuit layout to reduce the spurious capacitances and inductances'; no further detail
quantity: fitted parasitic addition to the feedback capacitance
value_as_stated: 'actual CF values: 0, 0.3, 0.3 and 0.4 pF with a parasitic addition of 0.2, 0.2, 0.1 and 0 pF (respectively)'
how_obtained: fitted to measured shot-noise spectra (0-100 MHz) within +/-1 dB. This survey solved the paper's Eq. (3) for C_F with the Table I values of f* and p and GBW = 3.9 GHz: total C_F = 0.173 +/- 0.018 pF for the bare 12-kOhm resistor; parasitic 0.26 +/- 0.05, 0.07 +/- 0.03 and 0.00 +/- 0.04 pF for the three cases with capacitors
verification: read on rendered PDF pages; recalculation in scripts_archive/parasitic_cf/inferred_feedback_c.py
confidence: medium for the bare-resistor case (0.17 pF); low for the others, which absorb the unknown tolerance of the 0.3-0.4 pF capacitors and an oscillation tendency at 2 kOhm
notes: The same fits give input capacitances (26 pF total) far above data-sheet values, so the single-pole model and parasitic bookkeeping carry systematic error.

source_title: What You Need to Know about Transimpedance Amplifiers - Part 1
layout: 'In order to minimize CPCB, remove the ground and power planes beneath the feedback trace between the amplifier's inverting input and output pin. Using resistors with small form factors, such as 0201 and 0402 reduces parasitic capacitance caused by the feedback components.'
quantity: qualitative guidance (feedback capacitor 'includes the parasitic capacitances from the printed circuit board and RF')
value_as_stated: p. 1: parasitic shunt capacitance 'may be as large as 0.2pF'
verification: read on rendered PDF pages
notes: Removing planes under the feedback trace lowers the capacitance from the summing node and output to ground; it does not shield the resistor ends from each other, so it can leave the end-to-end capacitance unchanged or slightly larger (compare the DC2414A and LTC6268 shielding results).

source_title: OPA818 data sheet, Feature Description: Feedback Pin; Layout Guidelines
amplifier_and_package: WSON-8 (DRG): 1 PD, 2 FB, 3 IN-, 4 IN+, 5 VS-, 6 NC, 7 OUT, 8 VS+, so FB sits directly next to IN- with no isolating NC pin; FB is tied to VOUT 'through metal routing on the silicon'. The SOT-23-5 (DBV) version has no FB pin and OUT (pin 1) and IN- (pin 4) are on opposite sides
layout: 'a very short feedback resistor (RF) connection between the FB and the IN- pins, thus minimizing parasitics'; 'Do not socket ... pin-to-pin capacitance introduced by the socket potentially creates an extremely troublesome parasitic network'
quantity: FB-to-IN- package coupling
value_as_stated: no value given
verification: pp. 3 and 15 read on rendered pages; the socket sentence on p. 24 located by text search
notes: Unlike OPA855/OPA858, the OPA818 has no NC pin between FB and IN-, so the direct pin-to-pin term is probably larger (this survey's expectation; no number is published).
